what: Plan section 7.30, not blind: the v2.1 rule 11 post-check for two-sided holding-company mergers, and stage 1 retrieval of MAE definitions in interpretation sections, 'Material Impact', and the terms an MAE definition names (prepare_v7.mae_definition_leaves); MAE re-extracted for the M11 and M12 agreements whose candidates changed, M11, M12 and the pool re-scored against the current gold.

m11holdout.248e37e8: Parent owned by Allscripts; no fees, no change
m11holdout.76955f6e: Company owned by Solstice; target fee moved to a reverse fee

m12holdout.7989f883: Parent owned jointly; sides recoded, reciprocal reverse fee dropped

schema_note: M11's re-extraction brief named schema v2.14; several M11 extractors and the M11 adjudicator also applied v2.15, which restates the MAE counting rules.

m11holdout.reason: 'Purchaser Material Adverse Effect' is capitalized and used operatively in the Purchaser bring-down (7.03(a)) though never defined, so it is present with not_stated fields (v2.1 rule 1) and adds a buyer-side entry beside Business Material Adverse Effect (v2.15 rule 1). The uses were in candidates.

m11holdout.correct_value: clause (iii) codes change_in_law, change_in_gaap and other
m11holdout.reason: Clause (iii) also carves out 'any development or effect of any investigation, audit or review' by a Governmental Entity, which no listed code covers, so it adds other; the extractor's own text named the investigations but dropped the code.

The definition states 'Solstice Termination Amount' means a cash amount equal to $14,500,000, a stated fixed figure. That definition line is not in candidates (S2 resolved definitions omit it), so the extractor could not see it.

Carve-out (z) excludes a disposition of the Alliance Interests 'in accordance with the terms of Section 7.1', the antitrust disposition Section 7.1(d) has the Company negotiate and effect; an action taken under the agreement's terms is compliance_with_agreement (same ruling as the earlier M11 adjudication of this item).

Clause (e) covers direct effects of compliance, including expenses 'relating to any litigation arising as a result of the Merger'; transaction litigation is stockholder_litigation whoever brings it (v2.11 rule 6). Nothing in it carves out announcement or pendency.

m11holdout.correct_value: clause (vii) codes announcement_or_pendency, stockholder_litigation and labor
m11holdout.reason: Clause (vii) also carves out 'any departure of any employee or officer of the Company' arising from the announcement; each clause takes every category it covers, and the M11 precedent codes employee-loss carve-outs as labor. Gold updated.

Only the Sellers' business MAE is defined; the Buyer litigation representation (Section 4.4) uses an undefined lowercase 'material adverse effect on the ability of such Buyer to perform its obligations' operatively, which v2.15 rule 1 says adds a buyer-side entry. Gold updated.

m12holdout.reason: Section 9.2 defines a generic 'Material Adverse Effect' for any entity, so the Target already has a defined MAE term; v2.15 rule 1 adds an entry only for a party with no defined MAE term of its own, so the lowercase 'material adverse change' in the Target MAC condition (6.3(f)) is not a third entry. The two entries are 'Material Adverse Effect' (both) and the 6.2(d) 'Material Adverse Change' (buyer_side).

m12holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, failure_to_meet_projections, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, natural_disaster, other, political_war_terrorism
m12holdout.reason: Carve-out (vii) reads 'war, material armed hostilities or other material international or national calamity or act of terrorism'; v2.3 rule 11 codes 'calamity' as natural_disaster (only 'crisis' in a war list is political_war_terrorism), so natural_disaster belongs beside political_war_terrorism.

m12holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, failure_to_meet_projections, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, natural_disaster, pandemic, political_war_terrorism, stock_price_or_volume
m12holdout.reason: Company T carve-out (D) excludes actions 'requested by the Transition Management Committee', a joint committee of one Company T and one Company Y representative whose requests must be unanimously approved in writing; the schema does not say whether a joint-committee request counts as one made at the buyer's request or with its consent, so gold's buyer_action_or_request is defensible but not compelled. Gold left unchanged.

m12holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, failure_to_meet_projections, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, natural_disaster, political_war_terrorism, stock_price_or_volume, stockholder_litigation
m12holdout.reason: Carve-out (h), 'the identity of, or facts relating to, Parent, Merger Sub or their Affiliates', is announcement_or_pendency under v2.5 rule 11, not other; no other carve-out in the Company MAE needs other.

m12holdout.correct_value: announcement_or_pendency, buyer_action_or_request, change_in_gaap, change_in_law, compliance_with_agreement, failure_to_meet_projections, financial_markets, general_economic, industry, natural_disaster, pandemic, political_war_terrorism
m12holdout.reason: Excluded Matter clause (c) is 'changes in financial, banking or securities markets in general, including ... any decline in the price of any security or any market index'; the price language illustrates market-wide changes and is not a carve-out for a decline in the party's own stock price or trading volume, so it is financial_markets only.

Clause (vi) covers omissions or actions taken with the Purchaser's consent, including those 'permitted by this Agreement'; permitted is not required, so it is buyer_action_or_request only, not compliance_with_agreement (v2.3 rule 11).

m12holdout.correct_value: 2 definitions (Material Adverse Effect target_side; undefined material adverse effect buyer_side); carve-out (b) general_economic + financial_markets
m12holdout.reason: The Sellers' bring-down condition on Buyer's representations uses an undefined lowercase 'material adverse effect on Buyer's ability to consummate', and Buyer has no defined MAE term, so it adds a buyer-side entry (v2.12 rule 3, v2.15 rule 1); the text is in the candidates. Clause (b) carves out changes in interest rates, a financial-market condition, beside general economic conditions, consistent with how both arms coded the same wording in 0a00167e.

Clause (H) carves out 'general national or international economic, financial, political or business conditions'; a bare 'financial' condition in a general-conditions list is general_economic (v2.3 rule 11 treats even 'market conditions' that way) and names no financial, credit or capital markets, so financial_markets is not added. Gold codes the same wording this way elsewhere in m12.

Clause (vii) carves out 'any resulting analyst downgrade of the Company's securities', an equity analyst rating that follows a missed projection, not a change in the Company's credit rating, so credit_rating does not apply; the clause stays failure_to_meet_projections and stock_price_or_volume.

The agreement separately defines 'Parent Material Adverse Effect' (an ability-to-perform definition) and uses it in Parent's representations; that definition is in the candidates, but the extractor said Parent has no defined MAE term.
